10.1e — 2-Button Jam: Polish

Polish is not decoration; it is COMMUNICATION AT 60 FPS. Every juice pass is the game answering the player's unasked questions: did that work? did it matter? can I do better? Today: sound, feedback, and the 30-second first impression — nothing new, everything better.

Polish Day ~50 min

The three passes (20 min each, from the wishlist ranked in 10.1d):

  1. The 30-second first impression. A new player decides about your game in half a minute: what do they SEE first (a title screen IS your first screen — name it, color it), what do they DO first (a 5-second safe beat before the first threat — 7.5a beat 1), what do they LEARN first (your two verbs, by doing them)?
  2. Feedback on everything. Every action needs a visible/audible answer: 
    verb pressed   → input feedback  (squash, flash, sound)
verb succeeded → reward         (coin sparkle, score pop)
verb failed    → consequence   (screen edge red, shake)
score gained   → number that MOVES (not a silent int)
    The starter taught you all of this: hit flashes (8.3a), coin destroy + count (2.1a), phase tints (8.2a). Reuse the tricks; they are yours.
  3. Sound. Three sounds minimum: an action sound (verb), a gain sound (reward), a lose sound (fail). Free sources with real licenses (9.10a rules): Kenney.nl assets, freesound.org with CC filters. A jam game with three sounds beats a silent one with twenty mechanics.

Freeze rule: last 10 minutes = NO new changes. Build (File → Build Settings), run the BUILD, not the editor. Build bugs (missing scene in build list!) are tomorrow's showcase killers — find them today.

Bug Hunt: Polish traps

  1. Your build runs but the build's scene list is empty — the classic jam disaster. Why do editor runs lie to you (what does the editor load that the build cannot)?
  2. Sound at full volume in a quiet lab. What is the right volume for showcase rooms — and why does volume get tuned AT the venue, not at home?
  3. A "polish" that adds a NEW mechanic appeared today. What does freeze mean — and what happens to untested mechanics on showcase day?
Close of Day ~5 min

Tinker: Showcase prep

  1. Build the final binary, put it on the desktop, name the file your GAME's name (not "build1"). Commit + push: "10.1e: polished build".
  2. Write the one-line pitch for 10.1f on a sticky note NEXT to the keyboard — that is your sign.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Show a 30-second first impression you designed
  • Give every action feedback a tester can see or hear
  • Ship three licensed sounds with credits in the repo
  • Run a frozen BUILD — not the editor — before leaving
